title: Porridge
subtitle: Scottish-style rolled oat porridge with milk and salt
excerpt: Rolled oats simmered slowly in a mixture of water and whole milk until thick and creamy, with just enough salt to bring out the oat flavour. The foundation breakfast. Toppings from honey to stewed fruit go on at the table.

recipe.sourceNotes: Porridge has been the staple breakfast of Scotland for centuries, made from whole or rolled oats cooked in water (the traditional method) or a mixture of water and milk. Salt is the traditional Scottish seasoning, added during cooking rather than at the table. The debate between the traditional water-only method and the richer milk version continues, but the water-and-milk method gives a creamier result without being heavy. Using rolled oats rather than jumbo oats produces a smoother porridge more quickly.

content.text: Stir constantly during the last 3 to 4 minutes of cooking: this is when the porridge thickens and catches on the base if left unattended. The salt goes in during cooking, not after: it becomes part of the oat flavour rather than sitting on top. The porridge will thicken further as it stands.
Put the oats, 300 ml of water, the milk, and the salt into a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring.
Reduce the heat to low. Cook for 5 to 8 minutes, stirring frequently, until the oats have absorbed the liquid and the porridge is thick and creamy. Add a splash more milk if it thickens too quickly.
Spoon into warm bowls. Drizzle with honey and add any other toppings at the table: sliced banana, a spoonful of jam, stewed fruit, or a scatter of seeds.
